Caledon seller: taking the chandelier?

What stays with a home is set by your agreement, so check before you list. 1) Check what your agreement lists as included in the sale. 2) Tell your Realtor® about anything you plan to keep, before you list. 3) Leave the keys, garage remotes and manuals for the new owners. 4) Leave the home empty of your belongings and as clean as your agreement requires. Ask your lawyer if you are unsure.

Mississauga: $2,500 rent for five years. What does it add up to?

Example only, simple arithmetic (same rent every month, no increases):
1) Year one: $2,500 x 12 = $30,000.
2) Years two and three: $30,000 x 2 = $60,000, so $90,000 so far.
3) Years four and five: $30,000 x 2 = $60,000, for $150,000 in total.
This is not a rent-vs-buy comparison: owning has its own costs, and real rents change.

Example only. Not mortgage, tax or legal advice.

caption:
Kitchener: buying with a friend? Plan the exit.

Buying with a friend or family member can work, but agree on the details first. 1) Agree who pays what, and how much, before you make an offer. 2) Decide what happens if one person wants out. 3) Ask a lawyer about a co-ownership agreement to put it in writing. 4) Ask your lender how several buyers are assessed together.
